F1_l2TestRootLeakage.note: the L2 gate allocates a real owned root (mkdtempSync under ~/.palimpsest-gates) and NEVER removes it: there is no rmSync of owned.root and every exit path funnels through finish() → process.exit(). The ONLY try/finally present restores the DSH_HOME env var around the worker run; it does not dispose the owned root. The P2-B rig's safeCleanup() exists but this gate never imports it. Measured: 22 leaked roots / 5.13 GB already present in the gate root (10 of them containing reparse points).

F2_junctionCleanupRisk.note: the P2-B safeCleanup() re-proves containment of the TOP-LEVEL owned root and refuses if the ROOT ITSELF is a reparse point, but it never inspects DESCENDANT reparse points before rmSync(recursive). The L2 gate copies the DSH profile's module tree with `dereference: true`, so the test home's node_modules contains REAL COPIES — but a leaked gate root can also contain a `node_modules` JUNCTION a previous run created, and a recursive rm follows it. The external-sentinel test (C2) is required to prove the actual mechanism.

F3_dependencyCopyCost.measuredMethod: du -sh on the resolved DSH module tree (the junctions dereference into ~518 MB)
F3_dependencyCopyCost.note: each L2 run builds TWO test homes (off + treatment), and each home's `profiles/node_modules` is populated by cpSync(dereference:true) over every entry of the real DSH module tree — measured at ~518 MB per copy, so ~1 GB per gate run, before sessions, SQLite and the world. This is the disk-exhaustion source; the size was measured, not inferred from package count.

F4_treatmentFailureLosesAssignment.note: the delivery provider returns bare `null` for EVERY refusal — no lineage, no qualified origin, an ambiguous/raced origin, an unavailable source, a durability mismatch, an over-budget Capsule and an invalid limit all collapse to the SAME null. The worker payload then forwards `?? null`, and the Host reports DELIVERY_DISABLED. There is NO assigned-arm field and NO eligibility field in any delivery contract, so a TREATMENT whose Capsule could not be materialized is indistinguishable from OFF at the worker boundary. This is exactly §8.2's forbidden substitution.

F5_controlReceivesHiddenCapsuleBody.note: the worker payload is `{ context, ... }` and `context` is the WHOLE WorkWorkerAttemptContext, whose `compiled.trajectoryCapsule.capsule` is the raw Capsule object. The payload is JSON.stringify'd verbatim into worker-context.json, so a CONTROL arm — whose presentation deliberately carries no history — STILL ships the full historical Capsule body in the Worker Environment. The rendered Prompt is clean; the environment is not. §8.6 forbids exactly this.

F6_controlDependsOnSuccessfulMaterializa.note: buildTrajectoryPresentation(CONTROL) itself needs no Capsule — the CONTROL section is a fixed constant. But the delivery PROVIDER builds the presentation only AFTER `capsuleForConsumer` returned AUTHORIZED, so if the origin Session Reader is unavailable and `capsuleForConsumer` refuses, the provider returns null BEFORE ever reaching the CONTROL branch. CONTROL's own no-history Section therefore disappears whenever materialization fails — the §8.8 defect.

F7_manuallyConstructedL2Presentation.note: the L2 gate bypasses EVERY product admission step: it hand-writes SECTION_TEXT, a fabricated capsuleDigest (`'a'.repeat(64)`), a fabricated consumerBasisDigest, an empty Capsule object `{}`, and passes the whole thing straight into the worker payload. It never calls capsuleForConsumer(), never calls buildTrajectoryPresentation(), never constructs a governed A0→A1 lineage and never reads a real Capsule. It therefore proves Host PLACEMENT of an operator-authored string — which is genuinely valuable — but proves NOTHING about product-rendered, source-qualified delivery.

F8_localDeterministicGenerationMiscounte.note: `providerRequestOccurred: false` is CORRECT for the external-provider sense (the adapter opens no socket and reads no credential), but the gate records it as an UNCONDITIONAL literal and never measures how many times the local adapter's `stream()` was actually invoked. A local generation request is therefore unmeasured, so a reader cannot tell 'no provider request' from 'no generation at all'. §14 Group E items 43/47 require the local invocation count to be measured separately.

F9_familyB_deliveryRefusal.note: confirmed in source: for `I-1 ASSOCIATION_QUALIFIED` + `I-2 OBSERVATION_INCOMPLETE` the qualified count is 1 but the total is 2, so selectInvocation returns AMBIGUOUS_REQUIRES_SELECTION, and capsuleForConsumer refuses with ORIGIN_NOT_SELECTED. This is an intentional fail-closed property (§10.1) and must NOT be weakened to make a benchmark run.

F10_noModelControlledInvocationSelector.note: a caller-supplied invocationId is a SELECTOR, not authority: it must be one of the ALREADY-QUALIFIED invocations or the request is refused (REQUESTED_NOT_QUALIFIED / REQUESTED_FOREIGN). A model cannot name an arbitrary Session to gain authority. The remaining gap (§8.4) is that `capsuleForConsumer` accepts a caller-supplied consumerAttemptId with no Host binding to `prepared.attemptId` — a canonical attempt's id can be passed by a wrapper. This is the selector-vs-authority boundary the E0 chain must bind.

F11_trialExposureNotReconstructable.note: the PALIMPSEST_WORKER_TRAJECTORY record carries state/placed/detail/deliveryState/sectionBytes/sectionDigest/userMessageDigest/userMessageBytes — genuinely useful delivery evidence — but NOT the assigned arm, NOT the eligibility basis and NOT the failure reason as a distinct class. The DSH SessionId exists on a SEPARATE PALIMPSEST_WORKER_SESSION_IDENTITY line, so the trial record alone cannot bind what arm was assigned to what was delivered to which Session; a reader must join two lines.

F12_hiddenTreatmentRetrievalPaths.note: a CONTROL worker can obtain the withheld Capsule through `environment.context.compiled.trajectoryCapsule.capsule` — the raw object is in the Worker Environment JSON regardless of the rendered prompt. It is NOT reachable through the Context Pull allowlist (that is derived from `compiled.handles`, and the Capsule is not a handle), but it IS present in the serialized worker-context.json the child reads. §8.6/§12 require the CONTROL child payload to omit it.

F13_informationSufficiency.note: the Capsule's per-event view carries seq/type/durability/inherited/summary/truncated, and the sanitizer builds summaries from STRUCTURAL fields only — raw tool arguments, raw tool results, assistant content and detailed failure causes are excluded. A `tool/result` event's `observedStatus` is NOT in the Capsule, so the Capsule cannot establish that a particular command SUCCEEDED or FAILED. §10.6: the benchmark must not claim the Capsule can prevent repeating a specific failed command unless the failure status is actually Capsule-visible.

F14_eventLevelProvenancePresentation.note: the Capsule ALREADY carries per-event `inherited`, `durability` and `truncated`, but the renderer emits only `[seq N] type: summary` per event. A benchmark that depends on whether events were inherited or truncated CANNOT see those facts in the model-visible Section. §10.7 permits adding ONLY the necessary already-verified labels — no raw content, no authority change.

F15_actualCanonicalSettlementFeasibility.note: the deterministic adapter reports READY_FOR_SETTLEMENT but performs NO Git work and modifies NO file. settleMutatingWork observes the real Git state and admits the basis before it exports and reports, so a READY_FOR_SETTLEMENT with an unchanged world is NOT a valid Origin Result. Establishing E0-L2 therefore requires the deterministic worker to make a REAL, allowed modification in a test-owned Git world and commit it through legitimate tooling — which the current adapter does not do. Whether that is safely achievable with existing facilities is investigated in C4; if not, E0-L2 is NOT_ESTABLISHED rather than fabricated.

F16_previousRegressionClassification.note: reconciliation of the P2-D2 broad-regression record: (a) the corrected P2-D1 real-integration gate raised its fixture budget 4096→8192 with an in-place §6.6 note because P2-D2's separated truncation metadata grew the Capsule essential floor — a real, understood change, and the test passes; (b) the two r3l0cr contract failures were reproduced at a baseline worktree and are pre-existing; (c) the mass failures during the first broad run were disk exhaustion on a full C: volume; (d) the node_modules damage was caused by `rm -rf` following a junction the operator created. The global test-hygiene sweep deletes ONLY `palimpsest-` prefixed temp dirs and does NOT follow reparse points — but it also does not CHECK for them, which is why C2 must add descendant-reparse inspection rather than rely on the prefix rule.
